title: AI and the Labor Market Productivity Driver or Job Killer
data_and_period: Germany social-insurance full-time20–64 excluding apprentices 2013Q1–2026Q1; EU-LFS full-time20–64 notin education2021Q1–2024Q4
measure_and_design: Eloundou exposure crosswalks; German continuous-exposure Poisson ageDDD; EUemployment and past12month newhires separately
main_finding: No broad exposed-occupation decline; German20–24relative weakness; EUautomation-weighted hiring signal
main_limit: German descriptive confounds remain; EUshortpreperiod; youngest comparison and survey coverage differ
comparison_to_our_results: Our November-anchored Norwegian youth signal is directionally similar; our multiplicity-adjusted evidence weaker and thresholds/ages/weights differ
policy_inference: Monitor labour-market entry separately from employment stocks

title: Labour Market Consequences of Generative AI Early Evidence from Norway
measure_and_design: Within-firm composition DID; occupation syntheticDID; firm shift-share
main_finding: Negative but small imprecise youth estimates; no robust displacement; backdated estimates often larger
main_limit: Availabilityshock notadoption; shortpost; specification and seculartrends
comparison_to_our_results: Our broad and dynamic estimates also do not establish robust causal displacement; laterpost includes2025reportingbreak
policy_inference: Use longpretrends and falsification before attributing displacement

title: Has AI Widened Employment Gaps Tracking Early-Career Employment by Occupational Exposure in Norway
measure_and_design: Complete occupational exposurequintiles and monthly employment comparisons
main_finding: Young complete-quintile contrast is an imprecise zero
main_limit: Exposurecomparisons notrandomised adoption; coverage and selectedoccupations matter
comparison_to_our_results: Our eight-county coarse2digitTHAIE proxy is a different estimand; completegroups and multiplicity constrain our signal
policy_inference: Do not infer allEurope displacement from selected occupations

title: Still Waters Rapid Currents Early Labor Market Transformation under Generative AI
data_and_period: Denmark adoption surveys linked to registers;11exposedoccupations; records throughDecember2024
main_finding: Task reorganisation and mobility precede mean earnings/hours effects; averageeffects over2percent ruledout in analysedwindow
comparison_to_our_results: A stock-level null is compatible with taskchange; our exposure alone cannot identify adoption effects
policy_inference: Link exposure with adoption training and workorganisation

title: Occupational exposure to generative AI firm adoption and labor market dynamics in France
type: LIFT Working Paper2026-02 and Banque deFrance note463
measure_and_design: ROME-based task index; age-specific contractflows; firm/sector-quarter comparison
main_finding: Young permanent-contract hires and separations weaken; firm totalemployment doesnotclearly diverge
main_limit: AIuse observedlate; monetary/tech/remote-work confounds; flows are notstocks
comparison_to_our_results: Our French annualsample composition doesnot measure hires and cannot replicate this mechanism
policy_inference: Monitor hires separations and training pipelines without treating countsasnetjobloss

title: Canaries in the Coal Mine Six Facts about the Recent Employment Effects of Artificial Intelligence
measure_and_design: Within-firm high-frequency exposure and age comparisons
main_finding: Earlycareer22–25relative weakness concentrated in automation and reducedhiring; no economy-wide displacement
main_limit: Descriptive authorscaution; educationattenuation; somepretrends; ADP selection versus nationalbenchmarks
comparison_to_our_results: Directional benchmark for our Norwegian <25signal only; cannot equate ages scores horizons or pointestimates
policy_inference: Separate entry hiring from incumbent outcomes and assess sample representativeness

title: Generative AI at Work
